commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

commands.name: doctor

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\loseu\Desktop\build-the-builder\.claude\skills\build-phone-agent

# Build a phone agent from a brief

Work from the kit folder. Use only what the brief and the tool API file say. Do not copy rules from another brief.

## Steps

1. Note the time: `date`. A build may take 30 minutes at most, tests included.
2. Read every brief file you were given in full, top to bottom. Do not search in it: a rule can sit in any paragraph. Then read `tools/openapi.json`. When a brief is raw material (a mail, a policy extract, a memo, a code list) instead of a numbered list of rules, write `tests/<slot>.facts.md` first: one numbered atomic fact per line with its file and date; a later record governs an earlier one (format in `docs/test-case-template.md`). `<slot>` is the brief's file name without `.md`.
3. Read `docs/workflow-format.md`, `docs/tools-and-code.md`, `docs/banking-customer-service-knowledge.md` and `docs/test-case-template.md`.
4. List the banking concepts in the brief: products, processes, terms, regulations. For each one that the knowledge file does not cover, research it with WebSearch and WebFetch before you write anything. Learn what it means, how banks usually handle it, and what an agent must never say or do about it. Keep it short: a few searches per concept. Then say in a line or two per concept what you found and where, and build the agent with it.
5. Read `examples/base-agent.json`. It is a small working agent with two steps. Use it as the pattern for the JSON, not as the answer.
6. Write the test cases before the workflow. `python3 tools/benchmark.py --fixtures` shows the practice customers whose bank data a case can borrow. Write `tests/<slot>.cases.json` from the brief, following `docs/test-case-template.md`. Check it: `python3 tools/benchmark.py --check --cases tests/<slot>.cases.json --rules <each brief file> [--rules tests/<slot>.facts.md]`. Fix every error. A passing check also writes `tests/<slot>.test-set.json`, the same cases with the fixture data merged in; it is derived, so never edit it, edit the cases file and check again. For each rule it lists as cited by no case, add a case, or note why no fixture can reach it. If it says the fixtures' identity fields are not in the tool API, the practice simulator cannot play identity for this brief: keep the third-party and callback cases (they still run), take the others out of the file, build the rest from the brief alone, and say so in your final line. Do not change `public-test-set.json`, `tools/openapi.json` or the tools, and do not bend the agent's identity step to fit the practice mock.
7. If `.freya-agents.json` already has an agent for this slot, or the brief builds on another brief whose agent is there, benchmark that agent first with step 10's command and its `agent_id`, before changing anything. What passes stays; rewrite only what fails.
8. Write the workflow to `out/<slot>.workflow.json`.
   - One step per stage of the call. Identity comes first.
   - Move to the next step on a tool result, not on what the customer says.
   - Take every tool field and allowed value from `tools/openapi.json`.
   - Validate every write in code before the tool call: the date against the calendar and the deadline, the amount against the floor and the full amount, the product id against what `get_account` returned. The model's own arithmetic never reaches the bank.
   - Leave `agent_config` out.
9. Save it: `python3 -c "import freya,json,sys; print(json.dumps(freya.save_workflow(sys.argv[1], json.load(open(sys.argv[2])))))" <slot> out/<slot>.workflow.json`
   It prints `workflow_id` and `agent_id`. The same slot updates the same workflow.
10. Benchmark it: `python3 tools/benchmark.py <agent_id> --cases tests/<slot>.cases.json --rules <the same files as in step 6>`. Add `--public A` when the brief is `briefs/brief-a.md` and `--public B` when it is `briefs/brief-b.md`, nothing otherwise: the public customers' expected records follow those two briefs and no other. A run takes 3 to 11 minutes. Run it in the foreground and wait for it to finish. Never start it in the background and never end your turn while a run is going: the builder stops when you stop.
11. Read `results/bench/<slot>/latest.md`, then `results/bench/<slot>/run-NN.transcripts.md`. Write `results/bench/<slot>/run-NN.review.md` (sections "Reading a benchmark report" and "Transcript review"). Fix the workflow file, save it again, benchmark again.
12. After every run, decide whether to run again (section "How many runs").
13. Finish with one line: the `workflow_id`, the `agent_id`, the score of the last full run (generated and public), how many runs you made, the rules no case reaches, and the brief points you could not settle.
14. Retrospective, only when the request says it is a practice run (section "Retrospective").

## Reading a benchmark report

- For each failed case, read the rules it cites again and decide: is the agent wrong, or the case? Public cases are never wrong. Change a generated case only when the brief shows its expectation is wrong, and say so in the review file. Never weaken a check or an expectation to make a run pass, and never test against anything but the real simulation.
- Find the cause in the transcript: the `↪` route lines, the `⚙` tool arguments and results, what the agent said just before.
- Fix the regressions first. Make the smallest fix; prefer routes, code and tool conditions over prompts.
- A flaky case counts as failing: the final runs every customer three times and counts only three passes.

## Transcript review

- After every full run, read `run-NN.transcripts.md`, passed cases too, against the whole brief, not only against the case's checks.
- For each case note: rules broken that no check named; anything the agent claimed without a tool result behind it (recorded, scheduled, transferred); turns a customer would find unclear; the turn before each hang-up; places where the customer's phrasing confused the agent.
- Write `results/bench/<slot>/run-NN.review.md`: one block per case with the findings, then the fixes you decided on, then the cases you will add for rules the run showed untested, then your decision about the next run and its reason.
- A finding from a passed case is fixed with the same priority as a failure: the final customers' checks are not yours.

## How many runs

- After every run you decide whether to run again, what to run, and when to stop. Decide from three things: the report's "What this run suggests" section, your transcript-review findings, and the clock. Write the decision and its reason at the end of the review file.
- A run takes 3 to 11 minutes. After a fix, re-run the failed cases with `--only`, then one full run before finishing to catch regressions.
- A benchmark command is cut off after 15 minutes. `--reps 2` on the full set fits only when the last full run took under 7 minutes; otherwise use `--reps 2` with `--only` on the flaky cases.
- One pass is a hint, not proof. When everything passes and time remains, run again (`--reps 2`, or a `--style` run) rather than stopping.
- Do not stop with time left while a case fails, is flaky, is untested after a change, or a review finding is unfixed.
- Stop when time is nearly out, when two consecutive full runs pass everything with no review findings, or when a fix round changed nothing.

## Banking knowledge

`docs/banking-customer-service-knowledge.md` holds general banking principles. Follow them in every agent you build.

- It gives principles, not values. Every rule, number, date, limit, identity question and outcome comes from the brief and `tools/openapi.json`. When the brief and that file disagree, the brief wins.
- When the brief says nothing about an action, do not invent a rule for it. Leave the action out, or hand the call off the way the brief allows.
- What you research (step 4) explains a concept. It never sets a rule or a value for this bank and never overrides the brief or `tools/openapi.json`. Research is not verification.
- What that file calls the "Guard MD" is the workflow's `system_prompt` and step prompts. Write it there, not in a separate file.
- Its process (section 14) is the steps above. Do not write role files or guard files. Test scenarios go in `tests/<slot>.cases.json` and nowhere else.
- Put its hard limits in routes, code and tool conditions, not only in prompts: no account data before identity passes, no success message before the tool result confirms it, no repeat of a write that timed out without checking first.
- Before each save, check the workflow against the "Final Design Principles" section of that file.

## Rules

- Never edit the agent on the platform by hand. Change the file and save it.
- When a tool call fails, the agent must say so. It must never tell the customer something is recorded when it is not.
- A customer that passes once can fail the next time. Prefer rules in routes and code over rules in prompts.
- An HTTP 5xx or a timeout from Freya or the bank is not a bug: it is transient. Wait a minute and run the same command again. Any other crash in `tools/benchmark.py` or `tools/trace_review.py` is a bug: say so in your final line. Do not edit the tools and do not test another way.

## Retrospective

Only when the request says it is a practice run.

1. `python3 tools/trace_review.py` writes `reports/<trace>.digest.md`, a digest of your own run so far: what you thought at each step (summarised), what you ran, what failed, how long each stretch took, commands you repeated, edits you never tested. Read it.
2. Write `reports/<slot>-retro.md` with: the score of every benchmark run of this build, in order; what cost time or turns, each with the digest's step number (a rule misread, a guess a test later contradicted, a repeated command, a tool error, a run started before `--check`); lessons that hold for any brief; lessons for this brief only, which never go into the skill; and, verbatim, the lesson lines you add to, change in or remove from this file.
3. Update the `## Lessons` section at the end of this file and nothing else in it: one line per lesson; general only — no rule, number, date, name, product, queue, outcome value or holiday from any brief; at most 12 lines; merge, replace or drop old lines rather than growing the list.

## Lessons

(none yet)

1	# Brief F: Freya Bank, application and request intake (BANK-004)
2	
3	Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer and application here is synthetic.
4	
5	This brief has the density of a real bank specification. Read all of it. The customer calls the bank; the agent answers the phone.
6	
7	## 1. The job
8	
9	Customers call to make an application or a request. The agent identifies the type, checks that it is supported, verifies identity, checks for an existing application of the same type, collects exactly the required fields, validates them, reads everything back, submits, and reports the application id. Receiving an application is not approving it. The agent decides nothing.
10	
11	## 2. Supported types
12	
13	| `type` | What it is |
14	|---|---|
15	| `card_replacement` | a new card to replace a damaged or expired card. A lost or stolen card is a security matter (rule 27), not an application. |
16	| `address_change` | a new postal address for the customer |
17	| `limit_increase` | a higher limit on a credit card |
18	
19	Anything else is unsupported (rule 3).
20	
21	## 3. Call variables
22	
23	| Variable | Example | Meaning |
24	|---|---|---|
25	| `customer_id` | `c_4f2a...` | The account matched to the calling number. Pass it to every tool call. The person on the line is not verified until section 5. |
26	| `first_name`, `last_name` | `Daniel`, `Reyes` | The account holder. |
27	| `title` | `Mr` or `Ms` | Address the customer as title plus last name once identity is verified. Before that, use no name. |
28	| `now` | `2026-10-14T11:00` | The current date and time. |
29	
30	## 4. Tools
31	
32	This brief's tool API is the table below. Field names and allowed values are exact; the agent sends nothing else. Every tool takes `customer_id`. A result with `ok: false` and an `error` means nothing was done. A 500 means nothing was recorded and the call may be repeated. Every call is written to the ledger the scorer reads.
33	
34	| Tool | Request fields | Result |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| `verify_identity` | `field`: `date_of_birth` or `phone_last4`; `answer` | `verified`, `wrong_answers_left`, `all_verified`, `hint` (`day_month_swapped`) |
37	| `get_requirements` | `type` | `fields`: list of `name`, `question` (the question to ask), `format` (`text`, `digits`, `amount`, `date`, `postcode`, `choice`), `options` (for `choice`), `required` (true or false). No identity needed. |
38	| `find_applications` | `type` | `applications`: list of `application_id`, `type`, `status` (`received`, `in_review`, `more_info_needed`, `approved`, `rejected`), `created_on`, `note` (text, may be empty). Refused until identity is verified. |
39	| `create_application` | `type`; `fields`: an object of field name to value | `application_id`, `status` (`received`). Refused until identity is verified. |
40	| `get_application` | `application_id` | `type`, `status`, `created_on`, `note`. Refused until identity is verified. |
41	| `transfer_to_agent` | `queue`: `applications`, `security`, `general` | `ok` |
42	| `close_call` | `outcome` (section 11); `reason` where the table lists one | `ok`. Always the last tool call. |
43

# Brief F: Freya Bank, application and request intake (BANK-004)

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer and application here is synthetic.

This brief has the density of a real bank specification. Read all of it. The customer calls the bank; the agent answers the phone.

## 1. The job

Customers call to make an application or a request. The agent identifies the type, checks that it is supported, verifies identity, checks for an existing application of the same type, collects exactly the required fields, validates them, reads everything back, submits, and reports the application id. Receiving an application is not approving it. The agent decides nothing.

## 2. Supported types

| `type` | What it is |
|---|---|
| `card_replacement` | a new card to replace a damaged or expired card. A lost or stolen card is a security matter (rule 27), not an application. |
| `address_change` | a new postal address for the customer |
| `limit_increase` | a higher limit on a credit card |

Anything else is unsupported (rule 3).

## 3. Call variables

| Variable | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | `c_4f2a...` | The account matched to the calling number. Pass it to every tool call. The person on the line is not verified until section 5. |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | `Daniel`, `Reyes` | The account holder. |
| `title` | `Mr` or `Ms` | Address the customer as title plus last name once identity is verified. Before that, use no name. |
| `now` | `2026-10-14T11:00` | The current date and time. |

## 4. Tools

This brief's tool API is the table below. Field names and allowed values are exact; the agent sends nothing else. Every tool takes `customer_id`. A result with `ok: false` and an `error` means nothing was done. A 500 means nothing was recorded and the call may be repeated. Every call is written to the ledger the scorer reads.

| Tool | Request fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `verify_identity` | `field`: `date_of_birth` or `phone_last4`; `answer` | `verified`, `wrong_answers_left`, `all_verified`, `hint` (`day_month_swapped`) |
| `get_requirements` | `type` | `fields`: list of `name`, `question` (the question to ask), `format` (`text`, `digits`, `amount`, `date`, `postcode`, `choice`), `options` (for `choice`), `required` (true or false). No identity needed. |
| `find_applications` | `type` | `applications`: list of `application_id`, `type`, `status` (`received`, `in_review`, `more_info_needed`, `approved`, `rejected`), `created_on`, `note` (text, may be empty). Refused until identity is verified. |
| `create_application` | `type`; `fields`: an object of field name to value | `application_id`, `status` (`received`). Refused until identity is verified. |
| `get_application` | `application_id` | `type`, `status`, `created_on`, `note`. Refused until identity is verified. |
| `transfer_to_agent` | `queue`: `applications`, `security`, `general` | `ok` |
| `close_call` | `outcome` (section 11); `reason` where the table lists one | `ok`. Always the last tool call. |

Formats: `digits` is digits only; `amount` is a number above zero with at most two decimals; `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way the customer said it, a date given only in numbers being day, then month, then year; `postcode` is exactly five digits; `choice` is one of `options`, matched by meaning to what the customer said.

## 5. Opening, type and identity

1. First sentence: "Thank you for calling Freya Bank. You are speaking with a digital assistant and this call is recorded. How can I help you today?"
2. Work out the type from the customer's words and name it back ("a replacement for your damaged card"). Ask at most two clarifying questions. A lost or stolen card is rule 27.
3. An unsupported type: say the digital assistant cannot take that application on this call and offer a transfer to the applications team. If the customer accepts, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `applications` and close as `transferred` / `applications`. If they decline, close as `no_action` / `unsupported`.
4. Several applications on one call: take them one at a time, in the order raised, each with its own existing-application check (section 6).
5. Every type touches customer data, so identity comes before `find_applications`, `create_application` and `get_application`. Ask two security questions, one at a time: the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file. Call `verify_identity` after each answer: `date_of_birth` as `YYYY-MM-DD`, `phone_last4` as four digits.
6. Three wrong answers in total end the check. Say the application cannot be taken on this call and that the customer can call back or visit a branch. Close as `not_verified` / `failed`.
7. `hint: "day_month_swapped"`: ask for the date again with the month as a word; that retry is not a wrong answer. `ok: false` with an error: ask the same question again; not a wrong answer either.
8. If the customer refuses the questions, explain once that they protect the account. If they still refuse, close as `not_verified` / `declined`.

## 6. Existing applications

9. After identity, call `find_applications` with the type. If an application with status `received`, `in_review` or `more_info_needed` exists, do not create another one. Say its `application_id` and its status in the words of rule 23.
10. For `more_info_needed`, read the `note` and say the applications team is waiting for that information. The agent cannot add it. Offer a transfer to the applications team; if the customer accepts, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `applications` and close as `transferred` / `applications`; if they decline, close as `status_given`.
11. An `approved` or `rejected` application does not block a new one.

## 7. Collecting the fields

12. Call `get_requirements` with the type. Ask the required fields in the order returned, one at a time, using the `question` text. Mention the optional fields once, together, and take them only if the customer offers them.
13. Check every answer against its format before moving on. If it does not fit, say what is expected and ask again. After three answers that do not fit the same field, offer a transfer to the applications team; if the customer declines, close as `no_action` / `incomplete`.
14. Never fill a field yourself, never guess, and never reuse a value given for another field.
15. For `limit_increase`, never state the current limit, the likely decision or a new limit. The requested amount is what the customer says, checked only against the `amount` format.
16. For `address_change`, do not read the old address aloud. Read back only the new one.
17. If the customer changes a value during collection or at the read-back, replace it and read it back again.
18. Do not ask for anything the requirements do not list, and never for a PIN, a password, a one-time code or a full card number.

## 8. Submitting

19. Read every collected field back and ask "Shall I submit this application?". Call `create_application` only after a clear yes.
20. Say the application is received only after `ok: true`. Read the `application_id` back digit by digit and say: "This means we have received it, not that it is approved. You will be informed within five business days by SMS."
21. If `create_application` times out or fails, do not repeat it at once. Call `find_applications` with the type first. If an application with today's `created_on` is there, it went through: report it as in rule 20 and do not create another. Otherwise call `create_application` once more. If that also fails, say the application was not submitted and offer a transfer to the applications team; if the customer accepts, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `applications` and close as `transferred` / `applications`; if they decline, close as `no_action` / `service_error`.
22. Never say an id the tool did not return.

## 9. Status enquiries

23. After identity, call `get_application` with the id the customer gives. Report the status in these words: `received` "received and waiting", `in_review` "being reviewed", `more_info_needed` "waiting for information from you", followed by the `note`, `approved` "approved", `rejected` "not approved". Give no reason the `note` does not contain and no date beyond "within five business days of the application".
24. If the id is not found (`ok: false`), say so and offer to look by type: call `find_applications` with the type the customer names and read the ids and statuses found. Never confirm an id you did not see in a tool result.

## 10. Other things customers say

25. A request for a person: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`.
26. Out of scope: anything that is not an application or a status enquiry, such as a balance, a payment, a transfer or a complaint. Say the digital assistant cannot do that and offer a transfer to the general team. If the customer accepts, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`. If they decline, close as `no_action` / `out_of_scope`.
27. A lost or stolen card, a transaction the customer does not recognise, or a code given to someone: ask for no details, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `security` at once, and close as `transferred` / `security`. Identity is not required first.
28. A question you cannot answer from the tools: say you do not have that information. Do not invent fees, dates or decisions.

## 11. Closing

29. Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason. It is the last tool call.

| Outcome | Reason | When |
|---|---|---|
| `application_created` | none | rules 20, 21 |
| `status_given` | none | rules 9, 10, 23, 24 |
| `transferred` | `applications`, `security`, `human` | rules 3, 10, 13 and 21; 27; 25 and 26 |
| `not_verified` | `failed`, `declined` | rules 6, 8 |
| `no_action` | `unsupported`, `incomplete`, `out_of_scope`, `service_error` | rules 3, 13, 26, 21 |

When several apply on one call: `transferred` wins; then `application_created`; then `status_given`; then `not_verified`; then `no_action`.

30. Before `close_call`, say in one sentence what was done and what the customer can expect, then thank them and say goodbye.

1	# Test cases for a phone agent
2	
3	The builder writes `tests/<slot>.cases.json` before it writes the workflow: a JSON list of cases, one per scenario, in the shape of `public-test-set.json` plus three fields. `tools/benchmark.py` checks the file, runs it against the agent on Freya's simulator and scores it the way the organisers do. `<slot>` is the brief's file name without `.md`.
4	
5	Every `--check` that passes, and every run, also writes `tests/<slot>.test-set.json`: the same cases with the fixture's `variables`, `identity`, `products` and `faults` merged in, in the key order of `public-test-set.json`, the generated fields (`fixture`, `rules`, `forbidden_tools`, ...) after them. It is derived: never edit it, edit the cases file and run `--check` again. It is what the simulator actually plays, and `python3 tools/run_cases.py <agent_id> --cases tests/<slot>.test-set.json` runs it with the kit's own runner.
6	
7	## How a case is played
8	
9	1. `benchmark.py` opens a session at the bank mock for the case's **fixture**, one of the 13 practice customers. The mock knows only those 13: their identity answers, products, amounts, `now` (`2026-10-14T11:00`, a Wednesday, the same for everyone) and, for PUB-10, a `create_promise` that fails the first time. `python3 tools/benchmark.py --fixtures` lists them with the product ids `get_account` returns (`p1`, `p2`, …).
10	2. A persona model plays the customer. It gets the fixture's name and identity answers and your `script`. It knows nothing else: not the brief, not the amounts, not the dates. It answers what it is asked and volunteers nothing; `run_cases.py` holds its exact instructions and the `style` variants.
11	3. The phone agent calls the bank's tools. Every call lands in the ledger.
12	4. Scoring. The ledger must equal `expected` exactly: outcome and reason, the set of promises, notes, callbacks and transfer queues; `close_call` must be the last call; `get_account` or `create_promise` before identity was verified fails the case; identity or account tools in a `not_reached` call fail it. A judge model reads the transcript against `checks`. Tools in `forbidden_tools` must not appear in the ledger. A case passes only when all of this holds.
13	
14	## The shape
15	
16	```json
17	{
18	  "id": "GEN-04",
19	  "fixture": "PUB-06",
20	  "title": "Haggles below the floor, then accepts the floor",
21	  "family": "Amounts",
22	  "level": "hard",
23	  "rules": ["brief-a:26", "brief-a:27"],
24	  "style": "corrects",
25	  "third_party": false,
26	  "script": "Verified. Cannot pay the full amount. Offers 50 today. When told that cannot be recorded, accepts the minimum payment today and confirms at the read-back.",
27	  "expected": {
28	    "outcome": "promise", "reason": null,
29	    "promises": [{"product_id": "p1", "amount": 637.5, "date": "2026-10-14"}],
30	    "notes": [], "callbacks": [], "transfers": []
31	  },
32	  "checks": ["the agent says 50 cannot be recorded", "the floor is offered once", "create_promise called exactly once"],
33	  "forbidden_tools": ["transfer_to_agent"]
34	}
35	```
36	
37	| Field | Required | Meaning |
38	|---|---|---|
39	| `id` | yes | Unique, `GEN-01`, `GEN-02`, … Never a public id. |
40	| `fixture` | yes | The practice customer whose bank data the case borrows. |
41	| `title` | yes | One line, what the customer does. |
42	| `family` | yes | The scenario family (see Coverage). Use `Third party` for someone else answering. |
43	| `level` | yes | `easy`, `medium` or `hard`. |
44	| `rules` | yes | The rules the expectation rests on, `<file-stem>:<number>`. |
45	| `script` | yes | What the customer does and says, in order, with every fact. |
46	| `expected` | yes | What the bank's records must show afterwards. |
47	| `checks` | yes | What the judge verifies in the transcript, one rule per line. |
48	| `style` | no | `pieces`, `corrects`, `talkative`, `asks_back` or `in_words`: how the customer talks. |
49	| `third_party` | no | `true` when someone other than the customer answers. |
50	| `forbidden_tools` | no | Tools that must never be called in this case. |
51	| `brief` | no | Only a tag; defaults to the fixture's brief letter. |
52	
53	Do not write `variables`, `identity`, `products` or `faults`: they come from the fixture and `--check` rejects them.
54	
55	## Choosing a fixture
56	
57	- The identity answers, products, amounts, days late and floor fields are the fixture's. A scenario about three products needs PUB-11 or PUB-12; two products, PUB-13; a failing promise service, PUB-10 and nothing else. PUB-10 always fails the first `create_promise`, so every PUB-10 case is a tool-failure case.
58	- Dates are computed from `now`, 14 October 2026, 11:00, a Wednesday, with the brief's calendar: its holidays, deadlines, bands and the meaning it gives to words like "next Friday". Write the resulting dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
59	- A fixture can carry several cases. `--fixtures` names the public case that uses it; write different scenarios, not copies of it.
60	
61	## Writing `script`
62	
63	- Say what the customer does, in order, with every number, date and answer they will say. The persona cannot invent anything: a fact that is not in the script does not exist for it.
64	- "Verified." is shorthand: the persona answers both identity questions correctly. For a failing identity, say which answers are wrong and how often ("gives 1987 as the year twice, then the right date").
65	- The persona discloses progressively. If the scenario needs the agent to ask something, write what the customer answers *when asked*, not that they say it on their own. That tests that the agent asks.
66	- "Confirms at the read-back" makes the persona say yes when the agent reads the promise back.
67	- For someone else answering, set `third_party: true` and say who answers and what they know ("her husband; offers to pay himself; says she is back tomorrow at eleven").
68	- Keep it to what matters; with a `style`, the persona pads the conversation itself.
69	
70	## Writing `expected`
71	
72	- `outcome` and `reason` exactly as the brief's outcome table and the tool API's values; `reason` is null only when the brief gives none for that outcome.
73	- `promises`: one per product with `product_id`, `amount` (a number, the amount the brief says gets recorded), `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Empty when no promise is recorded.
74	- `notes` (`product_id`, `reason`), `callbacks` (`date`, `time` as `HH:MM`), `transfers` (`queue`): empty lists when none.
75	- Everything is compared as a set with the ledger: an extra promise or a missing note fails the case.
76	
77	## Writing `checks`
78	
79	- One rule per line, observable in the transcript, with what the judge should look for: "the agent does not say the word 'collections' before both identity answers passed", "create_promise is called exactly once", "the read-back names both dates", "after the failed call the agent does not say 'recorded' until the retry succeeds".
80	- The judge sees only the transcript. No checks about internal state, and none about the ledger (that is `expected`'s job).
81	- The judge grades only what is listed, so a case can pass with violations no check names. The builder's transcript review covers those; `checks` are for the rules this case is about.
82	
83	## `rules`
84	
85	- `"brief-a:19"` is rule 19 of `briefs/brief-a.md`: the line that starts with `19.`. `python3 tools/benchmark.py --check --cases … --rules briefs/brief-a.md` lists the rules no case cites.
86	- When a brief is raw material with no numbered rules (a mail, a policy extract, a memo, a code list), write `tests/<slot>.facts.md` first: one numbered line per atomic fact, `12. <the fact> — <file>, <date>`. When two records disagree, the later dated one governs; say so in the line. Cite `"<slot>.facts:12"` and pass `--rules tests/<slot>.facts.md`.
87	
88	## Coverage
89	
90	- Every rule cited by at least one case, or named as unreachable with these fixtures in the builder's final line.
91	- Families to make sure of: happy path; identity failure (wrong answers, refusal); third party; date edges (the deadline, a weekend, a holiday, a vague period, "next" versus "this"); amount edges (the floor, below the floor, a partial amount); hardship; already paid; restructuring; tool failure (fixture PUB-10); a tool answer that needs care (`ok: false`, a `hint`, an error inside a 200 response); multi-product when the brief has it; a question outside the task; a customer who insists on something the brief does not allow; one or two `style` variants.
92	- 10 to 20 cases. One case may cite several rules. Prefer one case per decision branch over near-copies.
93	
94	## Two examples
95	
96	The examples follow Brief A and its practice customers. Your expectations follow your brief.
97	
98	Easy, fixture PUB-01 (Daniel Reyes, credit card ending 4821, 420.00 past due, 6 days late, minimum payment 126.00):
99	
100	```json
101	{
102	  "id": "GEN-01", "fixture": "PUB-01", "title": "Asks whether it is a robot, then pays in full on Friday", "family": "Happy path", "level": "easy",
103	  "rules": ["brief-a:4", "brief-a:28", "brief-a:19"],
104	  "script": "Asks whether he is talking to a robot, then confirms he is Daniel Reyes. Date of birth 14 March 1988, last four digits 4471. Cannot pay today. Can pay the full amount this Friday. Confirms at the read-back.",
105	  "expected": {"outcome": "promise", "reason": null, "promises": [{"product_id": "p1", "amount": 420.0, "date": "2026-10-16"}], "notes": [], "callbacks": [], "transfers": []},
106	  "checks": ["the agent says it is a digital assistant when asked whether it is a robot", "both security questions passed before get_account", "the read-back names Friday 16 October and 420"],
107	  "forbidden_tools": ["transfer_to_agent", "schedule_callback"]
108	}
109	```
110	
111	Hard, fixture PUB-13 (Elena Rossi; p1 credit card 300.00 past due, 4 days late, minimum 90.00; p2 personal loan 900.00 past due, 20 days late, instalment 300.00):
112	
113	```json
114	{
115	  "id": "GEN-09", "fixture": "PUB-13", "title": "Pays the card in full, cannot pay the loan", "family": "Multi-product", "level": "hard", "style": "in_words",
116	  "rules": ["brief-b:4", "brief-b:7", "brief-b:8"],
117	  "script": "Verified. Cannot pay everything today. For the credit card, can pay the full amount today. For the loan, says she cannot pay anything this month and refuses when offered the instalment. Confirms the card promise at the read-back.",
118	  "expected": {"outcome": "promise", "reason": null, "promises": [{"product_id": "p1", "amount": 300.0, "date": "2026-10-14"}], "notes": [{"product_id": "p2", "reason": "refused"}], "callbacks": [], "transfers": []},
119	  "checks": ["both products are stated before any amount is asked for", "the loan's instalment is offered once before the refusal is recorded", "the read-back names only the card promise", "add_note is called for the loan with reason refused"]
120	}
121	```

# Test cases for a phone agent

The builder writes `tests/<slot>.cases.json` before it writes the workflow: a JSON list of cases, one per scenario, in the shape of `public-test-set.json` plus three fields. `tools/benchmark.py` checks the file, runs it against the agent on Freya's simulator and scores it the way the organisers do. `<slot>` is the brief's file name without `.md`.

Every `--check` that passes, and every run, also writes `tests/<slot>.test-set.json`: the same cases with the fixture's `variables`, `identity`, `products` and `faults` merged in, in the key order of `public-test-set.json`, the generated fields (`fixture`, `rules`, `forbidden_tools`, ...) after them. It is derived: never edit it, edit the cases file and run `--check` again. It is what the simulator actually plays, and `python3 tools/run_cases.py <agent_id> --cases tests/<slot>.test-set.json` runs it with the kit's own runner.

## How a case is played

1. `benchmark.py` opens a session at the bank mock for the case's **fixture**, one of the 13 practice customers. The mock knows only those 13: their identity answers, products, amounts, `now` (`2026-10-14T11:00`, a Wednesday, the same for everyone) and, for PUB-10, a `create_promise` that fails the first time. `python3 tools/benchmark.py --fixtures` lists them with the product ids `get_account` returns (`p1`, `p2`, …).
2. A persona model plays the customer. It gets the fixture's name and identity answers and your `script`. It knows nothing else: not the brief, not the amounts, not the dates. It answers what it is asked and volunteers nothing; `run_cases.py` holds its exact instructions and the `style` variants.
3. The phone agent calls the bank's tools. Every call lands in the ledger.
4. Scoring. The ledger must equal `expected` exactly: outcome and reason, the set of promises, notes, callbacks and transfer queues; `close_call` must be the last call; `get_account` or `create_promise` before identity was verified fails the case; identity or account tools in a `not_reached` call fail it. A judge model reads the transcript against `checks`. Tools in `forbidden_tools` must not appear in the ledger. A case passes only when all of this holds.

## The shape

```json
{
  "id": "GEN-04",
  "fixture": "PUB-06",
  "title": "Haggles below the floor, then accepts the floor",
  "family": "Amounts",
  "level": "hard",
  "rules": ["brief-a:26", "brief-a:27"],
  "style": "corrects",
  "third_party": false,
  "script": "Verified. Cannot pay the full amount. Offers 50 today. When told that cannot be recorded, accepts the minimum payment today and confirms at the read-back.",
  "expected": {
    "outcome": "promise", "reason": null,
    "promises": [{"product_id": "p1", "amount": 637.5, "date": "2026-10-14"}],
    "notes": [], "callbacks": [], "transfers": []
  },
  "checks": ["the agent says 50 cannot be recorded", "the floor is offered once", "create_promise called exactly once"],
  "forbidden_tools": ["transfer_to_agent"]
}
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | Unique, `GEN-01`, `GEN-02`, … Never a public id. |
| `fixture` | yes | The practice customer whose bank data the case borrows. |
| `title` | yes | One line, what the customer does. |
| `family` | yes | The scenario family (see Coverage). Use `Third party` for someone else answering. |
| `level` | yes | `easy`, `medium` or `hard`. |
| `rules` | yes | The rules the expectation rests on, `<file-stem>:<number>`. |
| `script` | yes | What the customer does and says, in order, with every fact. |
| `expected` | yes | What the bank's records must show afterwards. |
| `checks` | yes | What the judge verifies in the transcript, one rule per line. |
| `style` | no | `pieces`, `corrects`, `talkative`, `asks_back` or `in_words`: how the customer talks. |
| `third_party` | no | `true` when someone other than the customer answers. |
| `forbidden_tools` | no | Tools that must never be called in this case. |
| `brief` | no | Only a tag; defaults to the fixture's brief letter. |

Do not write `variables`, `identity`, `products` or `faults`: they come from the fixture and `--check` rejects them.

## Choosing a fixture

- The identity answers, products, amounts, days late and floor fields are the fixture's. A scenario about three products needs PUB-11 or PUB-12; two products, PUB-13; a failing promise service, PUB-10 and nothing else. PUB-10 always fails the first `create_promise`, so every PUB-10 case is a tool-failure case.
- Dates are computed from `now`, 14 October 2026, 11:00, a Wednesday, with the brief's calendar: its holidays, deadlines, bands and the meaning it gives to words like "next Friday". Write the resulting dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- A fixture can carry several cases. `--fixtures` names the public case that uses it; write different scenarios, not copies of it.

## Writing `script`

- Say what the customer does, in order, with every number, date and answer they will say. The persona cannot invent anything: a fact that is not in the script does not exist for it.
- "Verified." is shorthand: the persona answers both identity questions correctly. For a failing identity, say which answers are wrong and how often ("gives 1987 as the year twice, then the right date").
- The persona discloses progressively. If the scenario needs the agent to ask something, write what the customer answers *when asked*, not that they say it on their own. That tests that the agent asks.
- "Confirms at the read-back" makes the persona say yes when the agent reads the promise back.
- For someone else answering, set `third_party: true` and say who answers and what they know ("her husband; offers to pay himself; says she is back tomorrow at eleven").
- Keep it to what matters; with a `style`, the persona pads the conversation itself.

## Writing `expected`

- `outcome` and `reason` exactly as the brief's outcome table and the tool API's values; `reason` is null only when the brief gives none for that outcome.
- `promises`: one per product with `product_id`, `amount` (a number, the amount the brief says gets recorded), `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Empty when no promise is recorded.
- `notes` (`product_id`, `reason`), `callbacks` (`date`, `time` as `HH:MM`), `transfers` (`queue`): empty lists when none.
- Everything is compared as a set with the ledger: an extra promise or a missing note fails the case.

## Writing `checks`

- One rule per line, observable in the transcript, with what the judge should look for: "the agent does not say the word 'collections' before both identity answers passed", "create_promise is called exactly once", "the read-back names both dates", "after the failed call the agent does not say 'recorded' until the retry succeeds".
- The judge sees only the transcript. No checks about internal state, and none about the ledger (that is `expected`'s job).
- The judge grades only what is listed, so a case can pass with violations no check names. The builder's transcript review covers those; `checks` are for the rules this case is about.

## `rules`

- `"brief-a:19"` is rule 19 of `briefs/brief-a.md`: the line that starts with `19.`. `python3 tools/benchmark.py --check --cases … --rules briefs/brief-a.md` lists the rules no case cites.
- When a brief is raw material with no numbered rules (a mail, a policy extract, a memo, a code list), write `tests/<slot>.facts.md` first: one numbered line per atomic fact, `12. <the fact> — <file>, <date>`. When two records disagree, the later dated one governs; say so in the line. Cite `"<slot>.facts:12"` and pass `--rules tests/<slot>.facts.md`.

## Coverage

- Every rule cited by at least one case, or named as unreachable with these fixtures in the builder's final line.
- Families to make sure of: happy path; identity failure (wrong answers, refusal); third party; date edges (the deadline, a weekend, a holiday, a vague period, "next" versus "this"); amount edges (the floor, below the floor, a partial amount); hardship; already paid; restructuring; tool failure (fixture PUB-10); a tool answer that needs care (`ok: false`, a `hint`, an error inside a 200 response); multi-product when the brief has it; a question outside the task; a customer who insists on something the brief does not allow; one or two `style` variants.
- 10 to 20 cases. One case may cite several rules. Prefer one case per decision branch over near-copies.

## Two examples

The examples follow Brief A and its practice customers. Your expectations follow your brief.

Easy, fixture PUB-01 (Daniel Reyes, credit card ending 4821, 420.00 past due, 6 days late, minimum payment 126.00):

```json
{
  "id": "GEN-01", "fixture": "PUB-01", "title": "Asks whether it is a robot, then pays in full on Friday", "family": "Happy path", "level": "easy",
  "rules": ["brief-a:4", "brief-a:28", "brief-a:19"],
  "script": "Asks whether he is talking to a robot, then confirms he is Daniel Reyes. Date of birth 14 March 1988, last four digits 4471. Cannot pay today. Can pay the full amount this Friday. Confirms at the read-back.",
  "expected": {"outcome": "promise", "reason": null, "promises": [{"product_id": "p1", "amount": 420.0, "date": "2026-10-16"}], "notes": [], "callbacks": [], "transfers": []},
  "checks": ["the agent says it is a digital assistant when asked whether it is a robot", "both security questions passed before get_account", "the read-back names Friday 16 October and 420"],
  "forbidden_tools": ["transfer_to_agent", "schedule_callback"]
}
```

Hard, fixture PUB-13 (Elena Rossi; p1 credit card 300.00 past due, 4 days late, minimum 90.00; p2 personal loan 900.00 past due, 20 days late, instalment 300.00):

```json
{
  "id": "GEN-09", "fixture": "PUB-13", "title": "Pays the card in full, cannot pay the loan", "family": "Multi-product", "level": "hard", "style": "in_words",
  "rules": ["brief-b:4", "brief-b:7", "brief-b:8"],
  "script": "Verified. Cannot pay everything today. For the credit card, can pay the full amount today. For the loan, says she cannot pay anything this month and refuses when offered the instalment. Confirms the card promise at the read-back.",
  "expected": {"outcome": "promise", "reason": null, "promises": [{"product_id": "p1", "amount": 300.0, "date": "2026-10-14"}], "notes": [{"product_id": "p2", "reason": "refused"}], "callbacks": [], "transfers": []},
  "checks": ["both products are stated before any amount is asked for", "the loan's instalment is offered once before the refusal is recorded", "the read-back names only the card promise", "add_note is called for the loan with reason refused"]
}
```
